definitions.explanation: A pattern of squares of two alternating colors, like a chessboard. Used on kimono cloth, floor tiles, wrapping paper, and design work generally.

examples.japanese: {市松模様|いちまつもよう}の{床|ゆか}。
{市松模様|いちまつもよう}の{着物|きもの}を{着|き}た{女性|じょせい}が{歩|ある}いていた。
examples.english: A woman in a checkered kimono was walking by.

examples.japanese: {東京|とうきょう}オリンピックのエンブレムには{藍色|あいいろ}の{市松模様|いちまつもよう}が{使|つか}われ、{日本|にほん}らしい{意匠|いしょう}だと{話題|わだい}になった。
examples.english: The Tokyo Olympics emblem used an indigo checkerboard pattern, and it drew attention as a distinctly Japanese design.

notes:
Formed from {市松|いちまつ} + {模様|もよう} (pattern). The name comes from the Edo-period kabuki actor Sanogawa Ichimatsu, who wore hakama in this pattern on stage and made it fashionable.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {市松模様|いちまつもよう}の{布|ぬの}: checkered cloth
- {市松模様|いちまつもよう}に{並|なら}べる: to arrange in a checkerboard pattern
- {白黒|しろくろ}の{市松模様|いちまつもよう}: a black-and-white checkerboard pattern

SIMILAR WORDS:
- チェック: check, plaid — the loanword, used mainly for woven cloth patterns with crossing lines
- {縞模様|しまもよう}: stripe pattern — parallel lines rather than alternating squares
